===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*leyp-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|leven}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lǣfan|t=to leave}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*laibijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*laibijaną|t=to let stay, leave}}, causative of {{m|gem-pro|*lībaną|t=to stay, remain}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leyp-|t=to stick; fat}}.

Cognate with {{cog|ofs|lēva|t=to leave}}, dialectal {{cog|nl|loven|t=to have left over, save, keep}}, {{cog|osx|lēvian}}, {{cog|goh|leiban|t=to leave}}, {{cog|non|leifa|t=to leave over}} (whence {{cog|is|leifa|t=to leave food uneaten}}, {{cog|sv|leva|t=to leave}}), {{m|is|lifna|t=to be left}} (whence {{cog|da|levne}}). More at [[lave#Etymology_2|lave]], [[belive#Etymology_1|belive]].

The noun is attested since the 19th century, with earliest references to billiards.

====Verb====
{{en-verb|~s|leaving|left}}

# To have a consequence or remnant.
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause or allow (something) to [[remain]] as [[available]]; to [[refrain]] from taking (something) away; to [[stop short]] of consuming or otherwise depleting (something) entirely.
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' my car at home and took a bus to work.}}
##: {{ux|en|The ants did not '''leave''' so much as a crumb of bread.}}
##: {{ux|en|There's not much food '''left'''. We'd better go to the shops.}}
##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=7|passage={{...}} St. Bede's at this period of its history was perhaps the poorest and most miserable parish in the East End of London. Close-packed, crushed by the buttressed height of the railway viaduct, rendered airless by huge walls of factories, it at once banished lively interest from a stranger's mind and '''left''' only a dull oppression of the spirit.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=May-June|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/david-van-tassel David Van Tassel]; [http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/lee-dehaan Lee DeHaan]
|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/3/wild-plants-to-the-rescue Wild Plants to the Rescue]
|volume=101|issue=3|magazine=w:American Scientist
|passage=Plant breeding is always a numbers game.{{nb...}}. The wild species we use are rich in genetic variation,{{nb...}}. In addition, we are looking for rare alleles, so the more plants we try, the better. These rarities may be new mutations, or they can be existing ones that are neutral—or are even selected against—in a wild population. A good example is mutations that disrupt seed dispersal, '''leaving''' the seeds on the heads long after they are ripe.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive|or|intransitive|copulative}} To cause, to result in.
##: {{ux|en|The lightning '''left''' her dazzled for several minutes.}}
##: {{ux|en|Infantile paralysis '''left''' him lame for the rest of his life.}}
##: {{ux|en|She '''left''' disappointed.}}
##: {{ux|en|The accident '''left''' the car a heap of twisted metal.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1899|author=w:Stephen Crane
|title=s:Twelve O'Clock|chapter=1
|passage=There was some laughter, and Roddle was '''left''' free to expand his ideas on the periodic visits of cowboys to the town. “Mason Rickets, he had ten big punkins a-sittin' in front of his store, an' them fellers from the Upside-down-F ranch shot 'em up{{nb...}}.”}}
##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=23|passage=The slightest effort made the patient cough. He would stand leaning on a stick and holding a hand to his side, and when the paroxysm had passed it '''left''' him shaking.}}
##* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-07-20|volume=408| issue=8845| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/http://www.economist.com/news/asia/21582043-villagers-enjoy-sunlight-after-dark-out-gloom Out of the gloom]| passage=[Rural solar plant] schemes are of little help to industry or other heavy users of electricity. Nor is solar power yet as cheap as the grid. For all that, the rapid arrival of electric light to Indian villages is long overdue. When the national grid suffers its next huge outage, as it did in July 2012 when hundreds of millions were '''left''' in the dark, look for specks of light in the villages.}}
## {{senseid|en|deposit (something) and withdraw oneself}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To put; to place; to deposit; to deliver, with a sense of withdrawing oneself.
##: {{ux|en|'''Leave''' your hat in the hall.}}
##: {{ux|en|We should '''leave''' the legal matters to lawyers.}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' my sewing and went to the window to watch the falling snow.}}
##* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|5|24|passage='''Leave''' there thy gift before the altar and go thy way.}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare King John|IV|iii|passage=The foot / That '''leaves''' the print of blood where'er it walks.}}
# To depart; to separate from.
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[let be]] or do without interference.
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' him to his reflections.}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''leave''' my hearers to judge.}}
##: {{ux|en|I'll '''leave''' it to you to decide.}}
## {{senseid|en|depart or depart from}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[depart]] from; to end one's connection or [[affiliation]] with.
##: {{ux|en|His bow and arrow never '''leave'''s him.}}
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' the country and I '''left''' my wife.}}
##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=1|passage=I was about to say that I had known the Celebrity from the time he wore kilts. But I see I will have to amend that, because he was not a celebrity then, nor, indeed, did he achieve fame until some time after I '''left''' New York for the West.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[end]] one's [[membership]] in (a group); to terminate one's affiliation with (an organization); to [[stop]] participating in (a project).
##: {{ux|en|I '''left''' the band.}}
## {{lb|en|euphemistic|transitive}} To [[die]] (the object denotes those affected by the death).
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To depart; to [[go away]] from a certain place or state.
##: {{syn|en|egress|q1=U.S., formal|absent|exit|make tracks|set forth|Thesaurus:leave}}
##: {{ux|en|I think you'd better '''leave'''.}}
# To transfer something.
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[transfer]] [[possession]] of after death.
##: {{ux|en|When my father died, he '''left''' me the house.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[intentionally]] [[place]] (something) to be received by another; to [[deliver]] (something) to a repository; to [[deposit]].
##: {{ux|en|I'll '''leave''' the car in the station so you can pick it up there.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To transfer [[responsibility]] or [[attention]] of (something) (to someone); to [[stop]] being [[concerned]] with.
##: {{ux|en|Can't we just '''leave''' this to the experts?}}
